- Según el Artículo 2, viajará a la ciudad con su gabinete la semana siguiente para presidir un consejo de seguridad.

## Por qué lo hizo
- **Violencia reciente.** Los textos mencionan:
  - un atentado con explosivos cerca del puente que une Cúcuta con Ureña (Venezuela), con varios heridos (tres, entre ellos policías, según el Artículo 2);
  - la incineración de un camión distribuidor de pollo en Villa del Rosario el 28 de octubre;
  - otros ataques en las últimas semanas.
- **Argumento oficial.** El presidente habló de combatir a "estructuras criminales y narcoterroristas" y dijo que no permitirá que "el narcoterrorismo siga sembrando el miedo".
- **Ubicación fronteriza.** Dijo que Norte de Santander es un departamento fronterizo y que el Estado debe garantizar "la seguridad y la soberanía".

## Diferencias entre los dos textos
- El Artículo 1 (Vanguardia) se centra en el atentado del puente y reproduce con más detalle el discurso presidencial.
- El Artículo 2 (RT) pone más énfasis en la frontera con Venezuela y menciona más hechos de violencia. También aclara que **la identificación de los responsables de cada hecho depende de las investigaciones** de las autoridades, y que la continuidad de la medida depende de la evolución del orden público.

**What happened**

Costa Rica officially inaugurated its first mega-prison, the Centro de Alta Contención contra el Crimen Organizado (CACCO), on a Wednesday in October. It sits in the La Reforma penitentiary complex in San Rafael de Alajuela.

- **Size and cost:** The site covers about 91,000 m² and cost ₡16.774 billion (₡16,774 million), according to Casa Presidencial. It is designed for roughly 5,100 inmates, in five independent modules of about 1,020 each.
- **Cells:** Each cell is about 90 m² and holds up to 60 people, with metal three-tier bunks. Toilet flush chains are placed outside the cells, and each cell has a patio for one hour of sun a day. Isolation cells can hold inmates for up to 48 hours.
- **Rules:** Inmates wear orange uniforms and cannot receive clothing from outside. Searches can happen at any hour. Lawyer and family visits take place behind glass with no physical contact. Four rooms are available for conjugal visits, which are allowed every two months for up to two hours and require a verified relationship and a social-work evaluation.
- **Staffing and first transfers:** At the start, about 30 administrative staff and more than 160 penitentiary police will work there. The Justice Minister, Gabriel Aguilar, said the first transfers will come at the end of October. They will be inmates from maximum-security areas who belong to criminal groups, along with identified "negative leaders."

**Why it was built**

- **Security crisis:** The government says crime has risen sharply and blames drug trafficking. The prison is meant to hold people linked to dangerous criminal structures, not "the common prisoner," in Aguilar's words.
- **Regional trend:** The prison follows the punitive model of El Salvador's Cecot. Nayib Bukele attended the groundbreaking and said it was modeled on Cecot. Other governments are moving the same way, with Ecuador's Noboa, Panama's Mulino and Peru's Keiko Fujimori announcing similar plans.
- **Perceived success of El Salvador:** Analyst Daniel Pontón says such prisons are presented as an alternative because El Salvador sharply reduced its crime indicators.

**Criticism**

Human rights groups and Pontón warn that this approach weakens the discourse of democracy, tolerance and human rights, and can lead to abuses. They point to Ecuador, where a mega-prison holds opposition figures such as Aquiles Álvarez and Jorge Glas. There have been complaints about denial of the right to a defense and about health care, and several inmates have died in state custody.

According to both articles, which summarize a New York Times report, a group of Arizona teenagers has become part of the supply chain that sends firearms to Mexican cartels.

**What happened**
- The Times interviewed four students in Arizona. They said they buy guns, which is legal in the U.S., and resell them to buyers tied to Mexican cartels, mainly the Sinaloa Cartel.
- They work largely from home, using messaging apps such as Telegram, WhatsApp and Signal.
- Some minors recruit older people to make the purchases. Others steal guns from their own homes. They advertise the weapons in encrypted channels.
- Once they find a buyer, they leave the guns at safe houses or hand them to cartel intermediaries, who take them to Mexico.
- They said they can earn thousands of dollars a month.

**Why they did it**
- **Money:** They learned from friends and social media that the market was large and lucrative. One said it was "easy" to make money.
- **Status:** One began buying guns to "be cool." Posing with firearms on social media also made them popular.
- **Hobby and easy access:** Some started buying guns as a pastime, and legal purchase in the U.S. made it simple.
- **Not coerced:** According to Article 2, they did not describe cartel recruitment or coercion. They also did not call themselves cartel members or claim loyalty to the group.

**Differences between the articles**
- Article 1 (Expansión) stresses that the teens are the cartels' "new and unexpected suppliers" and part of a "deadly international network."
- Article 2 (RT) emphasizes that they are not cartel members and were not forced into it. It also includes the reporter's description of them as typical American teenagers driven by money and status. RT is Russian state media, so its framing may serve its own interests, such as highlighting problems in the U.S.

Both articles are secondhand accounts of the Times report. The teens were anonymous and their claims are self-reported, so the full scale of the trafficking is not established by these articles.

On Wednesday, September 23, 2026, Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa addressed the UN General Assembly and proposed three actions against transnational organized crime.

**The three proposals**
1. **An international mechanism within the UN** to trace and freeze the illicit financial flows of transnational criminal groups. Noboa said that cutting off their financing requires acting in the countries through which their money moves.
2. **A permanent information-sharing platform** linking police forces, prosecutors' offices and financial intelligence units. He said this would let authorities anticipate criminal operations.
3. **Making organized crime a conflict-prevention priority under the UN80 initiative**, with the organization able to support states that request assistance.

**Why he made them**
- **The crime is transnational.** He argued that international cooperation must match the reach of criminal networks, whose operations cross borders. He cited arms trafficking through multiple countries, money laundering far from where crimes occur, and international routes for drug trafficking, human trafficking and illegal mining.
- **It is more than a police problem.** When these groups control territory and infiltrate institutions, they weaken state authority and the rule of law. When this happens in several countries at once, he said, it threatens international peace and security.
- **Safeguards on the help offered.** Assistance should be requested by states, respect their sovereignty and deliver measurable results. Ecuador said it is ready to push the proposals with other countries that want to join.

**Related themes in the speech**
- He linked security to education, business, investment and jobs, and asked that international financing account for the vulnerabilities of middle-income countries, not just per-capita income.
- He defended open, predictable and fair trade.
- He said illegal fishing threatens the Galápagos and illegal mining destroys Amazon forests and funds criminal groups, framing conservation as a security matter.
- He said AI could help education and productivity but could also deepen inequality or weaken institutions.
- He backed UN80 and the UN Charter and international law, and called for a UN better able to prevent and resolve crises.
- He also criticized what he saw as an imbalance between the criticism aimed at the fight against organized crime and the attention given to the crime's victims.

## What happened

- Ueno Bank became insolvent and was then placed under intervention. The articles don't say who intervened (presumably the financial regulator), and they give no details on why the bank failed.
- As a result, about G. 2 billion of the Cuerpo de Bomberos Voluntarios del Paraguay (CBVP) was immobilized. Of that, G. 1.4 billion came from the national annual fundraising drive and the rest was the institution's own money.
- About a year earlier, the CBVP had signed an agreement with Ueno Bank under which donations collected by fire stations nationwide were deposited into CBVP accounts there. The CBVP also uses other banks.
- The CBVP had 50 current accounts under a single legal entity. The guarantee covers only about G. 228 million per legal entity, not per account, so most of the money may not be recovered through the guarantee. The CBVP is seeking an exception and says it is "at the end of the list."
- CBVP president Lorena Canan says the freeze hurts operations across 140 stations and about 6,500 firefighters. Funds go to vehicle maintenance, station improvements and running costs. She is asking stations to stay calm.

## Why it happened

- **Direct cause:** the bank's insolvency and intervention, which the articles do not explain.
- **Why the CBVP was exposed:** it concentrated its fundraising proceeds in one bank, and the guarantee is capped per legal entity.
- **Canan's account of the warnings:** when rumors surfaced, she says Ueno manager Diana Mongelós assured her the bank was solvent and that the rumors were a "political question" meant to destabilize it. That claim is secondhand and unverified, and the bank's side is not heard in either article.

## Source reliability

- **The two articles are not independent.** RT's piece closely follows ABC Color's. The quotes and details are nearly identical, and a leftover placeholder ("citada por [medio]") suggests RT rewrote another outlet's report. RT therefore adds no real corroboration.
- **ABC Color** is a major Paraguayan newspaper and the likely original source. It is closer to the events and includes useful local context, such as service costs and the regulatory gap. Almost everything rests on one interview with Canan, an interested party, and there is no comment from Ueno, regulators or the central bank. It also has typos.
- **RT** is Russian state media, but this is a local financial story with little geopolitical angle, so distortion seems unlikely. Its framing ("víctimas" in quotes) is slightly more editorial, and its dollar conversions (about 6,150 guaraníes per dollar) look outdated compared with recent rates, so the dollar figures may be overstated. Rely on the guaraní amounts.
- Canan's feelings ("estafados") are opinion, not established fact. The amounts and the 50-account issue are also her claims and should be checked against the regulator or deposit-guarantee body.

**What happened**

Four Salvadoran soldiers, all air technicians (*aerotécnicos*) of the Fuerza de Tarea Libertad II, went missing after an ambush on Sunday. They were serving in the UN-authorized Gang Suppression Force (GSF) in Haiti and were returning to their camp in an armored vehicle.

- **The attack:** According to the Salvadoran armed forces, heavily armed criminal groups used firearms and explosives, which set off intense fighting. The armored vehicle was hit by explosives and caught fire, but all four soldiers got out.
- **Location:** The GSF said the attack took place in the Santo area of Croix-des-Bouquets, a commune in the West department about 12 km from Port-au-Prince.
- **Response:** RT adds that El Salvador sent several helicopters, which pushed the attackers back but were hit by gunfire. Other countries' contingents joined the effort. Attempts to reach the soldiers by land and air were hampered by the intensity of the fighting and the security conditions.
- **Current status:** The soldiers' whereabouts are unknown. Salvadoran and GSF forces are trying to make contact and locate them. The army said the situation is still developing.

**Why it happened**

Neither article gives a specific reason for this ambush. The context they give is:

- Armed gangs control most of Haiti's capital and carry out constant attacks and kidnappings that have displaced thousands of people.
- The UN Security Council created the GSF a year ago to combat the gangs and help stabilize the country. Its mandate was renewed for six months on September 29.
- The GSF has about 1,000 troops from El Salvador, Guatemala, Jamaica, Sri Lanka and Chad, under Mongolian Maj. Gen. Edernebat Batsuuri.
- According to the UN, gang violence has killed or wounded more than 5,700 people this year. The gangs are also blamed for more than 230 kidnappings and the rape of over a thousand women and girls.

The ambush therefore appears to be part of the gangs' violent resistance to the international force. That is an inference from the context, since neither article states a motive.

**Differences between the sources**

EFE gives the location, the GSF's confirmation and the wider background on Haiti's violence. RT gives more detail on the rescue attempts, including the helicopters that were fired on. Both rely mainly on the Salvadoran military's statement.

## What happened

On Saturday (September 26, 2026), Nicaragua's co-foreign minister, Valdrack Jaentschke, addressed the 81st UN General Assembly. According to both articles, he:

- **Expressed "firm and resounding solidarity with the heroic Cuban people."**
- **Backed China**, citing the "non-negotiable condition of one China," meaning Taiwan is not a separate state.
- **Backed Russia**, saying Nicaragua "shares and supports the fight against fascism and the right to peace of the Russian Federation."
- **Praised the BRICS countries** as the most populous and "perhaps most in solidarity" in the world, seeking better living conditions and "complementary development."
- **Called for peace ("paz, paz, paz")**, quoting the Nicaraguan poet Rubén Darío, and framed peace and harmony as necessary to overcome poverty and exploitation.
- According to RT, **condemned drug trafficking and organized crime** as "forms of terrorism" and called for more countries to join efforts on security, education, food, health, and development.

## Why

The articles give no explicit motive beyond what he stated. His stated rationale was that peace and harmony are prerequisites for fighting poverty. The rest of the speech fits Nicaragua's known alignment with Cuba, China, Russia, and BRICS. Jaentschke speaks for a government co-led by Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo, which is why his title is "co-foreign minister."

EFE adds context RT leaves out. On the same day, Cuban foreign minister Bruno Rodríguez told the Assembly that he hoped a US military intervention in Cuba would "never occur" and that Cuba would defend itself if one did. This suggests Nicaragua's solidarity statement came amid heightened US-Cuba tension, though EFE doesn't say Jaentschke was responding directly to it.

## Framing differences

- **EFE** includes the Cuban minister's remarks and notes the Ortega-Murillo co-presidency, which places the speech in a geopolitical context.
- **RT** emphasizes the peace and anti-crime themes, includes a tweet quoting the Russia line (calling Russia the "sister" federation), and omits the US-Cuba context. Its text is also cut off mid-sentence at the end.

# Destitución del canciller Manuel Tovar

## Qué ocurrió
- La presidenta de Costa Rica, Laura Fernández, destituyó a su ministro de Relaciones Exteriores y Culto, Manuel Tovar. Según el Artículo 1, fue un jueves; según el Artículo 2, la reunión fue el martes 22 de septiembre.
- Es la primera salida del Gobierno por despido, según el Artículo 2.
- Tovar estuvo 139 días en el cargo, desde mayo, según el Artículo 1. Citando medios locales, ese texto dice que es el canciller que menos ha durado desde 1948.
- Lo reemplaza Indiana Trejos Gallo, hasta ahora ministra de Comercio Exterior.

## Por qué lo destituyó
Según el comunicado oficial de Presidencia, Tovar gestionó "de manera inadecuada" la participación de Costa Rica en una sesión del **Escudo de las Américas**, en la que participó Donald Trump. El canciller asistió "sin dar aviso previo ni informar" a la presidenta.

El Artículo 1 añade que esto le impidió a Fernández participar en la sesión, lo que según el Gobierno causó "un gran daño de carácter estratégico". El Ejecutivo considera el Escudo de las Américas un espacio fundamental para la seguridad y la lucha contra el narcotráfico y el crimen organizado, y la seguridad es una de las prioridades de la presidenta.

## Contexto adicional (Artículo 2)
- El acuerdo del Escudo de las Américas lo firmó en Miami el ministro de Seguridad Mario Zamora, durante el gobierno anterior.
- Algunos sectores han advertido de posibles riesgos para la soberanía nacional y de una eventual presencia de fuerzas militares extranjeras en el país.

## Diferencias entre los dos textos
- **Sobre Trejos:** el Artículo 1 dice que ocupará el puesto sin más. El Artículo 2 la presenta como ministra *a.i.* (interina), mientras se define quién ocupará el cargo de forma permanente, y dice que asumirá cuando regrese de la Asamblea General de la ONU.
- **Sobre la reunión:** el Artículo 1 dice que Trump la encabezó. El Artículo 2 dice que la convocó el secretario de Estado estadounidense y que Trump participó.
- **Sobre el origen de los datos:** ambos se basan en el comunicado del Gobierno, así que la versión de Tovar no aparece en ninguno.

**What happened**

On Tuesday, October 27, at a rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, Trump said Venezuela could become the 51st US state. He proposed, "Let's make it the 51st state and, instead of a president, hold an election for a governor." The rally was in support of Republican candidates in the midterm elections.

**Why, according to the articles**

- **Oil:** Trump himself tied the idea to Venezuela's oil, saying "they have a lot of oil." Article 1 says this was his reason for the suggestion. He also said the US is receiving Venezuelan oil "at no cost to the American taxpayer," and described a shipment as the first of billions of barrels to come.
- **The new relationship and oil deal:** After the US military operation on January 3, which captured Nicolás Maduro, Washington restored diplomatic relations with Caracas. Trump thanked Venezuela's government for a deal giving the company North American Blue Energy Partners concessions on 17 oil fields. The Pentagon holds 35% of that company's parent firm. Article 2 says the deal gives the US access to about a fifth of Venezuela's crude reserves. Trump called relations "excellent" and said major oil companies are investing heavily.

**Differences in framing**

- Article 1 (RT) treats the remarks as a real annexation push. It stresses the casualties from the January bombings (over 100 dead) and describes Maduro's "kidnapping." It also notes that Trump has floated the idea before, including a "state 53" remark and a map posted on August 1. Acting president Delcy Rodríguez has repeatedly rejected it, citing Venezuela's independence and sovereignty.
- Article 2 (La Prensa) says Trump "joked" ("bromeó") and focuses on the oil deal. It also contains a fragment about a plan for Rodríguez to declare the presidency vacant, which would open a six-month window for elections, likely in 2027. The fragment is not explained.

Neither article reports any concrete steps toward making Venezuela a state. Whether the remark was a serious proposal or a joke depends on which outlet's framing you accept.

## What is reported

- **Who and where:** Fran Gregory Portillo Zapata, a 53-year-old Venezuelan man, died on October 29 at North Central Baptist Hospital in San Antonio, Texas, while in ICE custody.
- **Detention:** ICE arrested him on August 30. According to ICE's account (reported in Article 1), he was stopped while driving. After a "field interview," ICE decided he could be arrested administratively while his immigration case was still pending before the immigration court (EOIR). He was held at the Karnes County Immigration Processing Center.
- **Hospitalization:** He was admitted to the hospital on September 30 and stayed almost a month until he died.
- **ICE's stated medical explanation:** ICE says he had severe sepsis, acute pancreatitis and end-stage kidney disease. It says the official cause of death is pending further medical examination.
- **Notification:** ICE says it notified his immediate family and emailed the Venezuelan Embassy. Article 2 says the government did not publicly report the death until November 2.

## Disputed points

- **The family's account:** His sister, Liz Rocío Portillo Zapata, told Hispanos ATX that he had none of those conditions and that his only ailment was asthma. She says he had hired a lawyer, filed a habeas corpus petition and been granted asylum. The family demands justice, and the headline quotes the claim "they let him die."
- **Immigration history:** Article 1, the less reliable source, relays ICE's version. He was deported to Mexico in June 2023, tried to re-enter illegally in July 2023, was detained, and was then released on parole with a notice to appear before an immigration judge. Article 2 does not mention this history, and the sister's claim that he obtained asylum conflicts with ICE's portrayal of a pending deportation case. The articles don't resolve this.

## Why he died

The cause of death has not been established. ICE points to severe illness (sepsis, pancreatitis, kidney failure), but the final medical determination is pending. The family disputes that account and implies neglect or inadequate care, but neither article offers evidence of that. An autopsy, medical records or an independent investigation would be needed to settle it.

Article 2 adds context that about 60 immigrants have died in immigration custody, more than 30 of them Hispanic. Article 1 comes from a much less reliable source, so its details should be treated cautiously, though they mostly match ICE's own statement.

**Qué ocurrió**

Según un reportaje de *The New York Times* que recogen ambos medios, a partir de entrevistas con cuatro estudiantes de Arizona, algunos adolescentes estadounidenses se han convertido en proveedores de armas de los cárteles mexicanos, sobre todo del Cártel de Sinaloa. Este es el funcionamiento que describen:

- **Compra de armas:** empezaron comprando armas, en algunos casos como "pasatiempo", aprovechando la facilidad con que se adquieren legalmente en EE.UU. Los menores reclutan a personas mayores de edad para que las compren por ellos, y otros roban armas que encuentran en sus casas.
- **Contacto y venta:** se organizan casi sin salir de casa, con plataformas de mensajería como Telegram, WhatsApp y Signal, incluidos canales encriptados.
- **Entrega:** las dejan en casas de seguridad indicadas por los compradores o las pasan a intermediarios de los cárteles, que las llevan a México.

**Por qué lo hacen**

- **Dinero:** descubrieron que podían revender las armas a narcos mexicanos y ganar miles de dólares al mes. Uno de ellos mencionó lo "fácil" que resultaba ganar dinero.
- **Estatus social:** comenzaron para "ser cool", y en redes sociales ganaban popularidad al posar con armas.
- **Influencia del entorno:** uno se enteró por amigos y redes de que existía un gran mercado con mucho dinero circulando.

**Matices entre las fuentes**

Los dos artículos coinciden en lo esencial, pero el énfasis cambia. RT habla de "una mortífera red internacional" y destaca el papel de EE.UU. como fuente de armas. Expansión Política añade que los jóvenes no se consideran miembros del cártel ni le profesan lealtad, y que no describieron un sistema de reclutamiento forzoso por parte de los cárteles, sino que entraron por iniciativa propia. Todos pidieron el anonimato por la naturaleza criminal de sus actividades.

El reportaje retrata a los jóvenes como adolescentes típicos, preocupados por las chicas, las fiestas y el teléfono, a quienes los incentivos financieros les resultan demasiado poderosos a una edad tan temprana.

## Qué ocurrió

- El Gobierno de Javier Milei publicó el lunes 19 de octubre en el Boletín Oficial el **Decreto 1205/2026**, firmado también por el ministro de Defensa, Carlos Presti. El decreto declara **secreto militar** (en los términos del Decreto 9390/63) las operaciones contractuales para adquirir nuevo material y equipamiento para las Fuerzas Armadas.
- No se harán públicos el tipo de material, los costos ni la empresa proveedora. Los organismos contratantes seguirán con los trámites de compra, pero quedan **exceptuados de las normas de publicidad y difusión** del proceso.
- La Subsecretaría de Gestión Administrativa del Ministerio de Defensa se encargará de ejecutar los procedimientos.
- El decreto no fija plazos, montos ni etapas, y no vincula la compra con ningún programa concreto.
- No es la primera vez: antes se aplicó el secreto militar a la compra de los cazas F-16 (decretos de 2024 y el 735/2026).

## Por qué

- **Motivo oficial:** el Ministerio de Defensa sostiene que la naturaleza y la finalidad de la compra exigen que solo la conozcan personas autorizadas, porque divulgarla "podría comprometer la seguridad nacional y los medios de defensa de la Nación".
- **Contexto:** ambos medios sitúan la medida en medio de la tensión con el Reino Unido por las Malvinas. El Artículo 1, la fuente más fiable, menciona sanciones y denuncias contra petroleras no autorizadas, un arbitraje en la ONU contra el proyecto Sea Lion, la orden de construir una base naval en Tierra del Fuego, la protesta formal de Londres y la advertencia "implacable" del primer ministro Andy Burnham.

## Matices sobre las fuentes

- El decreto **no menciona expresamente las Malvinas**. Esa relación la establece la prensa como contexto, no el texto oficial.
- El Artículo 2, de menor fiabilidad, añade que la tensión se reavivó tras el Mundial, cuando los jugadores exhibieron una bandera con el lema "Las Malvinas son argentinas", y que Milei aprovechó políticamente el fervor nacionalista. Esto no aparece en el Artículo 1, así que conviene tomarlo con cautela. Además, su redacción es algo más valorativa (por ejemplo, "blinda").
- Los datos concretos del decreto (número, firmantes, contenido, antecedentes) provienen sobre todo del Artículo 1 y son coherentes con las citas textuales del Artículo 2.

# Renuncia de Santiago Peña, según los dos artículos

## Qué ocurrió
- Peña anunció su renuncia a la presidencia de Paraguay el jueves 5 de noviembre, mediante un mensaje en video a la nación.
- Pidió disculpas "si en algún momento" falló y dijo que nunca quiso defraudar la confianza de los ciudadanos.
- Aseguró que decidió pensando en la estabilidad del país, la paz social y la preservación de las instituciones democráticas. Añadió que "ningún cargo puede estar por encima del bienestar del Paraguay".
- Su prioridad, dijo, es la tranquilidad de quienes confiaron sus ahorros al sistema financiero. Pidió que se garantice la devolución de esos fondos, que el Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos cumpla su función y que se protejan los fondos públicos.
- Lo sustituirá el vicepresidente, Pedro Alliana. Peña había asumido en 2023 para un mandato que terminaba en 2028.

## Por qué renunció
1. **Crisis bancaria:** el martes anterior, el Banco Central intervino el Ueno Bank, una de las principales entidades del país, por insuficiencia de capital. Cerca de 3 millones de clientes quedaron sin acceso a su dinero.
2. **Sospechas de conflicto de intereses:** Peña había tenido acciones en un grupo que controlaba el banco, de las que se desvinculó en 2025. Aun así, la oposición lo acusó de conflicto de intereses y de favorecer a la entidad.
3. **Presión social:** hubo protestas durante dos noches seguidas en Asunción, con enfrentamientos con la policía, que usó gases lacrimógenos y camiones hidrantes.
4. **Fracaso de las medidas de contención:** el gobierno logró la renuncia del presidente del Banco Central y promulgó una ley de emergencia para devolver la mayor parte de los fondos en cinco días hábiles, pero eso no calmó el descontento.
5. **Pérdida de apoyo político:** el Partido Colorado, su propia agrupación, anunció que acompañaría el juicio político en el Congreso. Sin ese respaldo, Peña quedó sin margen de maniobra.

## Matiz entre las fuentes
El primer artículo explica las causas y el contexto político, y destaca la amenaza del juicio político. El segundo se centra en las palabras de Peña, que presenta su salida como un gesto por la estabilidad del país y no menciona el juicio político.

**What happened**

On Saturday (the article dates the tweet September 26, 2026), Nicaragua's co-foreign minister, Valdrack Jaentschke, spoke at the 81st UN General Assembly. Both articles report these main points:

- **Support for Cuba:** He expressed "firm and resounding solidarity with the heroic Cuban people." Article 1 places this alongside Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez's remarks the same day. Rodríguez said he hoped a US military intervention "never happens" and that Cuba would defend itself if one did.
- **Support for China:** He backed China's position on the "non-negotiable condition of one China," a reference to Taiwan.
- **Support for Russia:** He said Nicaragua "shares and supports the fight against fascism and the right to peace of the Russian Federation." This echoes Russia's own framing of its war in Ukraine.
- **BRICS:** He praised the growing strength of the BRICS countries, which he called the most populous and "perhaps most solidary" in the world, as a force for better living conditions and "solidary and complementary development."
- **Peace and poverty:** He called peace "the most important and fundamental of all battles" and urged the world to leave behind "poverty, misery and the exploitation of some by others." He quoted the Nicaraguan poet Rubén Darío: "paz, paz, paz."
- **Crime:** According to Article 2, he condemned drug trafficking and organized crime as "forms of terrorism" that strip societies of their wealth. He called for more countries to join efforts against them and to advance security, education, food, health and development.

**Why, based on the articles**

Neither article gives a detailed explanation, so some of this is inference.

- **Stated reasons:** He said Nicaragua came to the Assembly "with the force of the peace we believe possible" at home and worldwide. He argued that harmony is indispensable for fighting poverty. He framed the peace and development themes as the families' aspiration to live safely and build better societies.
- **Political alignment (inference):** The statements on Cuba, China, Russia and BRICS fit the foreign policy of the Ortega-Murillo government. Article 1 notes that Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo co-preside over it. The speech reaffirmed ties with these partners, which are anti-US or counter-Western in orientation. Además, RT amplía la cobertura a la granizada, las inundaciones y el caos vial.

En resumen, un episodio de viento intenso asociado a una tormenta convectiva, probablemente un tornado débil EF-0, dañó los techos del Terminal Sur. La clasificación oficial aún está pendiente.

- No se harán públicos el tipo de material, el costo ni el proveedor.

- **Motivo oficial:** el decreto sostiene que el contenido debe ser conocido solo por personas autorizadas, porque su divulgación "podría comprometer la seguridad nacional y los medios de defensa de la Nación". Ambos medios citan esta justificación casi textualmente.
- **Contexto que señalan los medios:** la medida llega en un momento de tensión con el Reino Unido por las Malvinas. La República menciona sanciones y denuncias contra petroleras no autorizadas, un arbitraje ante la ONU por el proyecto Sea Lion, la orden de construir una base naval en Tierra del Fuego, la protesta formal de Londres y la advertencia del primer ministro Andy Burnham. RT añade el efecto nacionalista de la protesta de los jugadores tras el partido del Mundial.

Ninguno de los textos citados del decreto menciona las Malvinas ni al Reino Unido. La relación causal es una **inferencia periodística basada en la coincidencia temporal**, no un hecho demostrado.

## Fiabilidad de las fuentes

- **La República (Colombia):** es un diario económico generalizado y no es parte del conflicto. Su artículo es más detallado y verificable: da número de decreto, firmantes, base legal, precedentes y contexto diplomático. Tiene un tono bastante neutral, aunque el texto copiado incluye restos de otras noticias ajenas al tema. Parece apoyarse en prensa argentina, no en reporte propio.
- **RT en Español (Rusia):** es un medio estatal ruso con intereses geopolíticos y antecedentes de sesgo, sobre todo contra gobiernos y potencias occidentales. Aquí las citas del decreto coinciden con las de La República, así que el núcleo factual parece sólido. Es menos fiable en el encuadre:

  - Presenta como hecho el episodio del Mundial, que no aparece en La República y que yo no puedo verificar.

## Conclusión

Lo bien corroborado es que se declaró secreto militar una compra de equipamiento sin revelar detalles, con la justificación oficial de proteger la seguridad nacional. Que la decisión responda a la tensión por las Malvinas es plausible, pero no está confirmado. Para detalles concretos conviene contrastar con el Boletín Oficial y con medios argentinos o internacionales independientes.

# Terremoto del 9 de octubre de 2026 en Panamá

## Qué ocurrió
- **Hora y lugar:** el sismo se produjo a las 12:56 (hora local) en la zona centro-sur de Panamá, cerca de Tonosí. Primicias ubica el epicentro en la localidad rural de Pitazola Arriba (distrito de Los Pozos, provincia de Herrera), en la costa del Pacífico.
- **Magnitud:** las cifras varían según la fuente (ver más abajo). Oscilan entre 7,2 y 7,7.
- **Réplicas:** hubo decenas, y según el Instituto de Geociencias (IGC), más de 100. Algunas llegaron a magnitud 6.
- **Tsunami:** el Servicio de Alerta de Tsunamis de EE. UU. emitió una advertencia para varios países del Pacífico. Después se dio por terminada la amenaza. Ecuador (Inocar) canceló su alerta a las 14:00 y Colombia dijo que no había amenaza.
- **Daños y víctimas:** no había balance oficial. Primicias, citando a Protección Civil, informa de al menos dos heridos y una persona atrapada en los escombros de una iglesia. Ambos medios mencionan daños en edificaciones, entre ellas la catedral de Penonomé. En San José (Costa Rica) hubo evacuaciones, pero no daños.
- **Servicios afectados:** hubo cortes de electricidad en varias provincias (Chiriquí, Herrera, Los Santos, Veraguas, Coclé y parte de Panamá Oeste) y problemas en plantas potabilizadoras por los fallos de energía.
- **Respuesta:**
  - El aeropuerto de Tocumen se evacuó, suspendió operaciones y las reanudó por la tarde tras inspecciones.
  - El Metro de Panamá cerró para evaluación estructural.
  - Se cerraron las oficinas públicas y se suspendieron las clases.
  - El presidente Mulino pidió calma.
  - El Canal de Panamá siguió operando con normalidad mientras inspeccionaba sus instalaciones.

## Diferencias entre las fuentes

| Dato | RT | Primicias |
|---|---|---|
| Magnitud | 7,2 inicial, luego 7,5 (IGC) | 7,7 en el titular; el USGS pasó de 8 preliminar a 7,6; el IGC dio entre 7,5 y 7,7 |
| Profundidad | 4 km (y 10 km en un reporte preliminar citado) | 10 km (USGS) |
| Ubicación | zona centro-occidental, 39 km de Tonosí | "sureste" de Panamá, aunque cita Herrera y Azuero, que están en el centro-sur |

Las diferencias son normales en las primeras horas, cuando las agencias revisan sus estimaciones. Primicias contiene además una inconsistencia interna: titula 7,7 pero cita al USGS con 7,6.

## Por qué ocurrió
Ninguno de los dos artículos explica la causa. Como contexto general (no proviene de los textos): Panamá se sitúa en una zona tectónicamente compleja, donde interactúan las placas de Cocos, Nazca, Caribe y el bloque o microplaca de Panamá. Allí se acumulan tensiones que se liberan en fallas y zonas de subducción. Para saber qué falla concreta se rompió habría que esperar el análisis de instituciones como el USGS o el IGC.

## Qué ocurrió

El martes 13 de octubre, tras el paso de un sistema frontal, la inestabilidad atmosférica en la Región Metropolitana generó tormentas con lluvia intensa, granizo, actividad eléctrica y ráfagas fuertes. En ese contexto, ráfagas de viento arrancaron partes de los techos y estructuras metálicas del Terminal Sur de buses, en Estación Central. Quedó registrado en videos ciudadanos.

La Dirección Meteorológica de Chile (DMC) hizo una evaluación **preliminar**: el fenómeno podría corresponder a un **tornado EF-0**, el nivel más bajo de la escala Fujita Mejorada, con vientos estimados de 105 a 137 km/h. Esa clasificación aún debe confirmarla el Departamento de Climatología, que no descarta que haya sido otro fenómeno. Una alternativa plausible, y esto es inferencia mía, sería una ráfaga descendente o un frente de ráfagas de la tormenta.

El temporal en general llevó a Senapred a declarar Alerta Roja en la región.

## Por qué ocurrió

La causa fue la nubosidad convectiva, es decir, tormentas intensas con características tornádicas. Los vientos de esas celdas, sean un tornado débil o ráfagas descendentes, fueron suficientes para levantar techumbres livianas.

## Fiabilidad de las fuentes

**Emol (artículo 1)**
- Es un medio generalista chileno, con cita directa de un meteorólogo y de la DMC.
- Mantiene los matices: "preliminarmente", "todavía tiene que estudiarlo" y "o fue otro tipo de fenómeno".
- Explica bien que la Alerta Roja respondió al conjunto de eventos y no solo al viento.
- Una debilidad es que los "daños leves" que cita parecen ser la descripción genérica de un EF-0, no una evaluación específica del Terminal Sur. Eso contrasta con las imágenes de techos desprendidos.

**RT en Español (artículo 2)**
- Es un medio estatal ruso. En un tema meteorológico sin carga política su información básica es coherente con la de Emol, porque se apoya en el tuit de MeteoChile, pero el tratamiento es más sensacionalista.
- El titular y el primer párrafo afirman que hubo un tornado ("Santiago en alerta roja por tornado"), aunque la DMC solo habló de una posibilidad preliminar. Además atribuye la alerta roja al tornado.
- Dice que el tornado "alcanzó" vientos de 105-137 km/h como si fueran mediciones, cuando son rangos estimados de la escala.
- Se apoya en tuits de cuentas poco verificables. Uno habla de "techos completos" y de "tornado / tromba", lo que contradice el carácter leve que describe la DMC.
- Califica la granizada de "histórica" sin respaldo de datos, usa un tono de espectáculo ("de película") y se equivoca con el nombre de la institución ("Servicio Meteorológico de Chile").
- Es más completo en los efectos urbanos (inundaciones, Metro, tráfico), pero sin fuentes oficiales para esos datos.

## Conclusión

Lo bien establecido es que hubo una tormenta severa y que ráfagas fuertes dañaron los techos del Terminal Sur. Que fue un tornado EF-0 es una hipótesis preliminar de la DMC, todavía sin confirmar. Para esto conviene fiarse más de Emol y de los comunicados de la DMC que de RT, cuyos titulares dan por confirmado lo que aún está en análisis.

**What happened (as reported):**
- On Saturday, October 17 (2026), Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, a 43-year-old lawyer and former anticorruption prosecutor, was shot dead while playing soccer at the Campo Marte sports complex in Guatemala City (zone 5).
- A second person was also killed, and at least five others were wounded (per EFE, citing local media).

**Why it happened:**
Nobody has established a motive. EFE says the circumstances and possible motives are still under investigation, and RT gives no motive either. The following is background, not a finding about cause:

- EFE frames him as a prominent anticorruption figure and emphasizes the official condemnations. RT emphasizes his legal troubles and gives fewer details about the investigation.
- RT says the second victim was not immediately identified, and describes the detentions as preliminary.
- The motive remains unknown, and the suspects' claims and any links to the killing have not been verified.

**What happened**

Ueno Bank became insolvent and was then taken over (intervened) by the authorities. As a result, about G. 2,000 million (roughly US$325,000) belonging to the Cuerpo de Bomberos Voluntarios del Paraguay (CBVP) was frozen. Of that sum:

- G. 1,400 million (over US$227,000) came from the annual national fundraising drive (*colecta nacional*).
- The remaining amount was the institution's own funds.

**Why the money was there**

- About a year ago the CBVP signed an agreement with Ueno Bank for the national collection. Everything the fire stations raised nationwide went into CBVP accounts at that bank.
- The CBVP also works with other banks. Article 2 adds that Ueno was linked to two collections, the latest in October.

**Why recovery is a worry**

- The CBVP had 50 current accounts under a single legal entity.
- The deposit guarantee is only about G. 228 million (about US$37,000) per legal entity, not per account. That covers only a small part of the frozen funds.
- The CBVP is near the end of the repayment list. It is exploring whether an exception can be made and is checking which administrative avenues it can use.

**The warnings they received**

When rumors about the bank's condition began, CBVP president Lorena Canan asked Ueno manager Diana Mongelós, who had negotiated the agreement. Mongelós said the bank was solvent, that nothing would happen, and that it was only a "political matter" meant to destabilize the bank. Canan now says: "Y ahora nos encontramos en esta situación."

**Impact**

- Canan said the CBVP feels "dolidos y estafados" and asked the stations to stay calm.
- The freeze hurts operations across the 140 stations and roughly 6,500 firefighters. The funds pay for vehicle maintenance and repairs, structural improvements, and operating costs.
- Article 2 notes that the money was public donations, which Canan said hurts the most. It also gives sample service costs: about G. 1.5 million for a vehicle-accident rescue with ambulance transport, G. 5 million for a vehicle fire, and up to G. 350 million for a major fire.
- Stations are calling constantly, and uncertainty is total.

**Note on the sources**

Both articles report the same core facts and quotes. Article 2 adds the operating-cost details and the mention of two collections. Article 2's text also has some inconsistent figures, such as "G. 2 mil milones" in one place, which most likely means G. 2,000 million.

Según ambos medios, el martes la Oficina de Control de Activos Extranjeros (OFAC), del Departamento del Tesoro de EE.UU., anunció un endurecimiento de las sanciones contra Cuba. Las medidas principales son:

Los textos no citan una justificación oficial del Tesoro, pero el contexto que ofrecen apunta a estos motivos:

- **Política de "máxima presión" de Trump.** Según AFP, Washington no oculta que desea un cambio de régimen en La Habana. Trump considera que Cuba es una "amenaza extraordinaria" para la seguridad de EE.UU. y ha hablado de "tomar el control" de la isla. Ya había aplicado un bloqueo petrolero de facto desde enero.

- AFP señala que las medidas llegan cuando las importaciones privadas cubanas desde EE.UU. se disparan: 149 millones de dólares en julio, el máximo mensual desde 1992.

## Diferencias de enfoque entre las fuentes

A very strong earthquake struck Panama at 12:56 local time on Friday, October 9, 2026.

- **Magnitude:** Reports vary. Panama's Instituto de Geociencias (IGC) first said 7.2, then 7.5, and one preliminary report said 7.0. Primicias cites the USGS at 7.7, after an initial estimate of 8 and a revision to 7.6. The IGC later gave a range of 7.5 to 7.7.
- **Location:** The epicenter was in south-central Panama, about 39 km west of Tonosí. Primicias places it near the rural locality of Pitaloza/Pitazola Arriba in Herrera province. It was shallow, at 4 to 10 km depending on the source.
- **Aftershocks:** More than 100 followed, with magnitudes up to about 6.0.
- **Damage and casualties:** There was no official toll as of the reports. Civil protection sources cited at least two injured and one person trapped in the rubble of a church. Videos showed severe damage to some buildings, including the cathedral in Penonomé. Buildings were evacuated in Panama City and San José, Costa Rica.
- **Infrastructure:**
  - Power outages hit Chiriquí, Herrera, Los Santos, Veraguas, Coclé and part of Panamá Oeste. These disrupted water treatment plants.
  - Tocumen airport was evacuated, then resumed operations after inspections found no significant damage.
  - The Metro was evacuated and shut down for structural checks.
  - The Panama Canal kept operating while it inspected its facilities.
- **Tsunami:** The US tsunami warning system issued an alert for Pacific coasts from Mexico to Peru. It was later lifted, and Ecuador's Inocar canceled its alert at 14:00.
- **Government response:** President Mulino called for calm and warned against using the event to spread alarm. He closed public offices so officials could contact relatives, and the Education Ministry suspended classes for the rest of the day.

## Why it happened

Neither article explains the cause. The quake was shallow and in a tectonically active region, where several plates and microplates meet. That suggests a tectonic origin, but the articles don't identify the fault or mechanism, so I can't say more with confidence.

The sources also disagree on magnitude, depth and location (for example "center-west" versus "southeast"), which is normal for early reporting. The figures are likely to be refined.

On Wednesday, September 23, 2026, Ecuador's president, Daniel Noboa, addressed the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. It was his first in-person speech at the forum since taking office in late 2023. Both articles agree on the substance of the three proposals he presented.

**The three proposals**
1. **A UN international mechanism** to trace and freeze the illicit financial flows of transnational criminal groups. Noboa argued that cutting off their financing requires acting in the countries where the money circulates.
2. **A permanent information-sharing platform** for police, prosecutors and financial intelligence units, so that states can anticipate criminal operations instead of reacting to them.
3. **Including transnational organized crime in the UN80 reform initiative** as a "conflict prevention priority." The UN would also be given the capacity to support states that request help.

Noboa said Ecuador is willing to push these proposals with any countries that want to join.

**Why he made them**
- **Criminal networks cooperate better than states.** He said criminals share routes, logistics, finances and technology "without red tape, without distrust and without delays," and that no state can defeat "an enemy that doesn't recognize borders." He called it inadmissible that criminal organizations cooperate more effectively than states.
- **Organized crime is more than a policing problem.** According to El Comercio, he argued that when these groups control territory and infiltrate institutions, they weaken state authority and the rule of law. When this happens in several countries at once, it threatens international peace and security. He cited arms trafficking, money laundering, drug routes, human trafficking and illegal mining.
- **Security underpins development.** He tied security to education, business, investment and jobs. He also asked that international cooperation and financing take into account the vulnerabilities of middle-income countries. On Tuesday, October 13, a storm hit Santiago, and videos showed roofs and metal structures being torn off the Terminal Sur bus station in the Estación Central district. Corrugated zinc sheets and other debris were blown across the area where the buses park. Emergency crews were reported at the site.

**Why it happened**

Chile's Dirección Meteorológica (MeteoChile/DMC) preliminarily attributed the damage to convective cloud with tornadic characteristics, possibly an EF-0 tornado. EF-0 is the weakest category on the Enhanced Fujita scale. The agency estimated winds of 105 to 137 km/h. The storm occurred during post-frontal instability, which also brought heavy rain, hail, lightning and power outages to many parts of the Metropolitan Region.

**Caveats**

- The classification is preliminary. Meteorologist Elio Brufort said the climatology department still has to study the event and confirm whether it was a tornado or some other phenomenon.
- The articles differ in how they describe the damage. Emol quotes the DMC as calling the damage "light": fallen tiles, small roof pieces torn off, damaged gutters and cladding, broken branches and uprooted shallow-rooted trees. RT's account stresses "entire roofs" being blown off and calls the scene a "disaster." Those descriptions are hard to reconcile, and the video-based accounts may reflect the most dramatic damage at the terminal rather than the DMC's overall assessment.
- Both articles say the DMC's wind range and EF-0 rating came from the agency, but neither explains the basis for them. The sources are social media videos and a preliminary assessment, not a completed survey.

**Wider impact**

Senapred declared a Red Alert for the whole Metropolitan Region. There was also historic hail, flooding from overwhelmed drains, traffic chaos, and suspension of some Metro stations and public transport routes. Sernageomin warned of a moderate-to-high chance of debris flows and landslides in the Andean foothills.

## What happened

- **Timing and size:** A strong earthquake struck southern-central Panama on Friday, October 9, 2026, at 12:56 local time. Magnitude estimates varied by source (see below), but both articles put it at roughly 7.5-7.7.

## Why it happened

Neither article explains the cause. As general background not drawn from them, Panama sits where several tectonic plates and microplates meet (Cocos, Nazca, Caribbean and the Panama block). Their interaction, including along the Panama Fracture Zone off the southern coast, makes the region seismically active. The specific fault and mechanism for this event would need confirmation from USGS or the IGC.

Según ambos medios, la presidenta Laura Fernández destituyó al canciller Manuel Tovar. El motivo oficial es que Tovar asistió a una sesión del "Escudo de las Américas", una coalición de seguridad contra el narcotráfico promovida por EE.UU. y en la que participó Donald Trump, **sin avisar ni informar a la presidenta**. Según el Gobierno, eso le impidió a ella participar y causó un "gran daño estratégico". La cartera pasa a Indiana Trejos Gallo, ministra de Comercio Exterior.

## Dónde coinciden (y por tanto es más fiable)

- La destitución y su motivo oficial, con la misma cita del comunicado de Presidencia.
- El nombre de la sustituta.
- La importancia que el Gobierno da al Escudo de las Américas en seguridad.

## Diferencias y matices

| Aspecto | RT | La República |
|---|---|---|
| Sustitución | Presentada como definitiva ("su lugar lo ocupará") | Trejos es ministra **a.i.** (interina), asumirá al volver de la ONU y la titularidad permanente "se define" |
| Trump | Lo describe como quien "encabezó" la reunión | La sesión fue convocada por el secretario de Estado, y Trump participó |
| Contexto | Casi ninguno | El acuerdo lo firmó en Miami el ministro de Seguridad del gobierno anterior, Mario Zamora, y hay críticas por la soberanía y una posible presencia militar extranjera |
| Datos exclusivos | Los 139 días de Tovar y el récord de brevedad desde 1948 (atribuido a "medios locales", sin citarlos) | La fecha de la reunión (martes 22 de septiembre) y que es la primera salida por despido del Gobierno |

Los 139 días son coherentes con las fechas, pero el récord desde 1948 no lo confirma el otro medio.

## Fiabilidad

- **RT** es un medio estatal ruso, con tendencia a encuadrar con sesgo los temas de EE.UU. y América Latina. Aquí el texto es bastante fiel al comunicado, pero omite contexto relevante, como las críticas al acuerdo y su origen en el gobierno anterior. Su titular simplifica ("por no avisarle de una reunión con Trump").
- **La República** es un diario costarricense, más cercano a los hechos y con más contexto. Pero es una "noticia en desarrollo", tiene descuidos de edición (un "Cortesía/[medio]" sin completar, redacción repetitiva) y también depende casi por completo del comunicado oficial.

## Conclusión

Lo bien establecido es que Fernández destituyó a Tovar y que el **motivo oficial** es haber asistido a la reunión sin informarla. Lo que **no** se puede afirmar con estos textos es si hubo otras razones políticas, como discrepancias sobre el Escudo de las Américas, ni cuál es la versión de Tovar, que ninguno recoge. Ambos artículos reproducen la versión del Gobierno, así que conviene contrastarla con más fuentes, como otros medios costarricenses, el comunicado original de Presidencia y una declaración de Tovar. Yo tampoco puedo verificar estos hechos de forma independiente.

**What happened**

Ueno Bank became insolvent and was intervened by the authorities. As a result, about G. 2,000 million (roughly US$325,000) belonging to the Cuerpo de Bomberos Voluntarios del Paraguay (CBVP) was frozen. Of that amount:
- G. 1,400 million came from the organization's annual national fundraising drive (the *colecta nacional*).
- The remaining sum was the institution's own funds.

**Why the funds were there**

About a year earlier, the CBVP signed an agreement with Ueno Bank for the national collection. Under it, everything the fire stations raised across the country was deposited into CBVP accounts at that bank. The CBVP also works with other banks. According to ABC Color, Ueno was tied to two collections, the latest in October.

**Why the situation is serious**

- The CBVP had 50 checking accounts under a single legal entity. The deposit guarantee covers only about G. 228 million (about US$37,000) per legal entity, not per account. So only a small part of the money may be recovered under current rules.
- The CBVP says it is near the end of the list of creditors. It is asking whether an exception can be made and is reviewing administrative options for an appeal.
- The freeze affects operations at its 140 stations and roughly 6,500 firefighters. The money pays for vehicle maintenance and repair, station improvements, and running costs. President Lorena Canan said the stations are anxious and calling constantly, and she has asked them to stay calm. She also stressed that the money came from citizens' donations.

**The bank's earlier assurances**

When rumors about the bank's trouble began, Canan asked Ueno manager Diana Mongelós, who had negotiated the agreement. Mongelós said the bank was solvent and that the rumors were a "political matter" meant to destabilize it. Canan now says the CBVP feels "hurt and cheated" (*dolidos y estafados*).

**Differences between the articles**

Both articles rely on the same statements from Canan and are largely consistent. RT frames the firefighters as "victims" and gives US dollar conversions. ABC Color adds detail on the cost of fire and rescue services, for example G. 1.5 million for a vehicle accident response and G. 350 million for a major fire. It also reports that the CBVP has been left in a "complicated" position to provide service.

Neither article explains in detail why Ueno Bank became insolvent. They only report the intervention and the bank's claim that the rumors were politically motivated.

## What happened

Both outlets agree on the core facts. On Tuesday, 27 October, at a rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, Donald Trump said Venezuela should become the 51st US state and elect a governor instead of a president. The rally was held to support Republican candidates in the midterm elections. He made the remarks while praising the new US-Venezuela relationship, which he called "excellent," and the oil arrangements that came out of it.

## Why, according to the articles

- **Oil is the stated motive.** RT quotes Trump saying "Tienen muchísimo petróleo" and boasting that the US is extracting large amounts of Venezuelan oil "at no cost to the US taxpayer."
- **The oil deal gives context.** EFE reports that Trump thanked Venezuela for a deal giving North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) concessions over 17 oil fields. The Pentagon holds a 35% stake in NABEP's parent company, and the deal reportedly gives the US access to about a fifth of Venezuela's crude reserves.
- **The background is the US operation against Maduro.** Both outlets say Maduro was removed in a US military operation in January. After that, Washington restored diplomatic relations with Venezuela under acting president Delcy Rodríguez. EFE's text also hints at a plan involving reforms, a vacated presidency and elections, probably in 2027, but the excerpt is fragmentary.

## Differences and reliability

**RT (Russian state media)** is the more slanted source.
- It frames the remarks as "annexation pretensions."
- It uses loaded terms such as "bombings," "kidnapping" of Maduro, and "more than 100 dead."
- It leaves out the NABEP and Pentagon details, which would complicate a simple "annexation for oil" story.
- It does add useful background: Trump's earlier "53rd state" remark, the map he posted labeled "state 51," and Rodríguez's repeated rejections. These are attributed and plausible, but I can't verify them independently.

**EFE (Spanish news agency)** is generally more reliable and neutral.
- It uses less charged language ("capture," "military intervention").
- It supplies concrete deal details.
- It says Trump "bromeó" (joked). That is an interpretation and may understate his seriousness, given that he has repeated the idea and posted a map.
- The text you gave appears truncated, so some context is missing.

## Bottom line

Trump publicly floated making oil-rich Venezuela a US state at a midterm campaign rally, tied to US oil interests there. Whether it was a joke or a real aim is unclear. EFE's account is the more dependable on the facts, and RT is useful mainly for the history of the remarks, which should be read with its anti-US slant in mind.

## Where the articles conflict

| Point | Article 1 (Contexto Tucumán) | Article 2 (RT) |
|---|---|---|
| Where Flávio went | Entered Argentina at 22:50 Tuesday, then flew from Puerto Iguazú to Guayaquil, Ecuador | Reportedly arrived in the US, perhaps Florida, and met his brother Eduardo |
| Timing of Trump's remarks | Early Wednesday, at Joint Base Andrews | Tuesday night |
| Trump on Colombia | Not mentioned | Says he took sides in Colombia but not in Brazil |

## Reliability

- **Contexto Tucumán** is a regional Argentine outlet. Its account is more checkable: it cites an official statement from Argentina's immigration agency, plus the aircraft type and registration and departure times. Those details are hard to square with Article 2's claim that Flávio was already in the US on Tuesday evening. It also gives fuller Trump quotes, including ones less flattering to Brazil's process. Its weakness is that it likely relies on secondary reporting for the flight details.
- **RT en Español** is Russian state media, which tends to frame Western and Latin American politics through its own editorial lens. Its Trump quotes match the other article, so that part seems sound. But its claim that Flávio arrived in the US rests on unnamed sources and on other outlets (The Washington Post, Metrópoles), and it isn't confirmed. It also omits the Argentine immigration evidence and Trump's remark accepting the final result.

**Bottom line:** Trump's statements are consistent across both sources. He said he'd welcome Flávio and doubted how the election was run, but he didn't claim to know where Flávio was. The claim that Flávio reached the US is weakly supported. The Argentine documentation points to him being in transit through Argentina to Ecuador. I can't independently verify any of these events, so this assessment rests only on how well each article supports its claims.
